bullets: What a balanced diet must supply, how food releases its energy, and the pipeline that breaks food down and absorbs it
slides.heading: Nutrition: balanced diet and digestion
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we check what a balanced diet must cover, weigh food as fuel, then follow one meal from the mouth to the large intestine - and catch the scene that corrects a famous stomach myth.

bullets: Name the seven food groups of a balanced diet and compare the energy released per gram by carbohydrate, protein and fat
Trace food through the gut, match each enzyme to the one nutrient it breaks down, and correct the claim that digestion finishes in the stomach
slides.heading: What we will learn
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud slowly and tell the class: the stomach is only one stop on the pipeline, and our exit ticket will ask you to prove what happens after it.

bullets: The stomach churns food for hours and gets all the attention, so it feels like the main event
So is digestion finished when food leaves the stomach - or has the real work barely started?
slides.heading: Is the stomach the finish line?
slides.notes: Ask the class: where does digestion finish? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because scene 6 puts the stomach claim on trial.

bullets: A balanced diet covers seven food groups: carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre and water
Digestion is a pipeline: food is broken down stage by stage from the mouth to the large intestine
Most digestion and nearly all absorption happen in the small intestine, through the villi
slides.heading: Diet in, digestion through
slides.notes: Stress the pipeline picture: each organ does one stage of the job, and the small intestine - not the stomach - is where food finally enters the blood.

bullets: Carbohydrates, proteins and fats supply energy and building materials; vitamins and minerals protect and regulate
Fibre keeps food moving through the gut and water is the solvent every process runs in
slides.heading: A balanced diet covers all seven food groups
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and name each group as it lands: energy, growth and repair, protection, movement, solvent.

bullets: Carbohydrate and protein each release about 17 kJ per gram
Fat releases about 37 kJ per gram - more than twice as much, which is why fatty food is energy-dense
slides.heading: Food is fuel: energy content per gram
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and pause on the fat bar: ask why a small portion of fatty food can carry more energy than a large portion of carbohydrate.

bullets: The mouth chews and starts starch digestion, then the oesophagus pushes food to the stomach
The stomach churns food into a liquid, the small intestine finishes digestion and absorbs, and the large intestine absorbs water
slides.heading: The digestion pipeline: mouth to large intestine
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and trace one bite along the whole route, naming each organ's one stage as the food passes it.

bullets: Amylase breaks down starch, protease breaks down protein and lipase breaks down fat
Each enzyme is specific: the wrong enzyme cannot do another enzyme's job
slides.heading: Enzymes: each one breaks down one nutrient
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and match each enzyme to its nutrient as the pairs lock together: amylase to starch, protease to protein, lipase to fat.

bullets: Villi cover the small intestine wall and give it a huge surface area
Digested nutrients pass through the villi into the blood, which carries them to the body cells
slides.heading: Villi in the small intestine absorb the nutrients
slides.notes: Play scene 5 and zoom on the villi: a folded, finger-covered wall absorbs far more than a smooth tube could.

bullets: Food leaves the stomach only partly digested: enzymes in the small intestine finish the breakdown
Most digestion and absorption continue in the small intestine, long after the stomach's turn
slides.heading: Misconception: digestion does NOT end in the stomach
slides.notes: Play scene 6 and ask the class to state the correction in one sentence: digestion continues in the small intestine, where most absorption happens.

bullets: Suppose a sandwich leaves the stomach as a soupy liquid, its starch only partly broken down
In the small intestine, enzymes finish breaking down starch, protein and fat, and the villi absorb the products into the blood - so digestion finishes there, not in the stomach
slides.heading: Worked example: where does a sandwich finish digesting?
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, the stomach churns and starts the job. Step 2, the small intestine finishes digestion and absorbs, so the finish line is the small intestine.

bullets: In pairs: list the organs one bite passes through, in order, and name what happens at each stop
Then swap and check: did anyone end digestion at the stomach?
slides.heading: Your turn: trace one bite
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the stomach named as the finish, then take two pairs' full routes.

bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says digestion finishes in the stomach
Name what continues in the small intestine and where absorption happens to earn full credit
slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers follow the food past the stomach to the villi.
